transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Corva Coleman.
President Trump is in Shenzhen, China, where he is meeting other leaders for the Asia-Pacific
Economic Cooperation Forum, but many are waiting for his conversation later with Chinese leader
Xi Jinping and what they might discuss about trade.
NPR's Jennifer Pack says Trump and Xi are meeting for the third time this year.
What's been happening between these leaders' summit is a lot of back and forth.
The U.S. has accused China of still restricting the flow of rare earths.
These are critical in the production of everything from cell phones to weapons.
And then the Trump administration has been adding more Chinese firms and universities
on blacklists.
So just this week, the U.S. Commerce Department had blocked the remote access of the most
advanced U.S. chips, like from Nvidia.
And that will have a huge impact on Chinese AI firms on the cutting edge.
Ben Pierre's Jennifer Pack reporting from Shenzhen.
Meanwhile, Russian President Vladimir Putin is expected to join Trump and Xi for the discussion.
The Associated Press has called the outstanding Senate race in Alaska for Democratic challenger
Mary Peltola.
She defeated Republican incumbent Dan S. Sullivan with slightly more than 50 percent of the vote.
Peltola released a video statement thanking supporters and promising to get to work.
We need to fight corruption and corporate greed.
We need to bring prices down.
We need to lower fuel costs and build new homes.
And we need to ensure that Alaskans are served by your elected senators.
There are a handful of House races the A.P. has not yet called.
That includes Alaska's lone House race, Republican incumbent Nick Begich currently leads.
On Capitol Hill today, House Democrats will hold their leadership elections.
The winner of that election is likely to become the next speaker of the House.
The governments of Kuwait and Bahrain say Iran launched attacks on their territories
early today.
This comes as the International Maritime Organization reports Iran's attacks on ships in the Strait
of Hormuz have hit record highs.
And Pierre's Aya Batrawi has the latest.
Iran says it targeted U.S. air defense systems in Kuwait, while Bahrain confirmed more Iranian
attacks.
Iran described these latest attacks as defensive.
Iranian media reports several days of U.S. strikes on an Iranian island in the Strait
of Hormuz.
U.S. Central Command has not responded to requests for comment.
Meanwhile, Iran says it struck two ships on Tuesday, including a liquefied gas tanker that
exploded into a ball of fire in the Strait of Hormuz.
Indian officials say the 24 Indian seafarers had to jump into the water.
Oman's Navy confirmed their rescue.
Abu Dhabi's National Oil Company says 11 crew members were hospitalized and that one
remains missing following an attack on one of its ships, but it did not name the vessel.
Aya Batrawi, NPR News, Dubai.
You're listening to NPR News.
The Justice Department has unsealed charges against an Irish man who was accused of wrecking
parts of a U.S. war plane in Ireland.
Federal prosecutors say that in April, the man got through a security perimeter at Shannon
Airport in western Ireland.
It often houses U.S. military planes.
The man allegedly used an axe on a C-130 Hercules aircraft and allegedly cut hydraulic lines
and smashed cockpit gauges, among other damage.
The Irish man is not yet under arrest.
Online safety advocates and legal experts testified yesterday at a Senate Judiciary
Subcommittee hearing.
NPR's Ritu Chatterjee reports they focused on the popular gaming platform Roblox and
the risks for children.
The hearing was held by the Subcommittee on Crime and Counterterrorism, which is chaired
by Republican Senator Josh Hawley of Missouri.
If your children are on Roblox, they are being exposed in all likelihood to sexual predators,
to sexually obscene material, to sexually exploitative content left, right and center.
Witnesses said that Roblox prevents users and their families from suing the company through
an arbitration clause that children unwittingly agree to when they sign onto the platform.
Earlier this week, Holly and Democratic Senator and Ranking Member Dick Durbin of Illinois
introduced a bipartisan legislation that would allow families of minors who've been exploited
online to go to court.
Ritu Chatterjee, NPR News.

topics.text: Trump meets Chinese leader Xi in Shenzhen amid disputes over rare earths and chip restrictions
Associated Press calls Alaska Senate race for Democrat Mary Peltola over Republican Dan Sullivan
House Democrats hold leadership elections, with the winner likely to become next Speaker
Kuwait and Bahrain say Iran launched attacks on their territories, amid Strait of Hormuz ship attacks
Iran strikes liquefied gas tanker in Strait of Hormuz; Indian seafarers rescued, Abu Dhabi ship crew missing
Justice Department charges Irish man with sabotaging U.S. C-130 aircraft at Shannon Airport
Senate Judiciary subcommittee hearing examines child safety risks on Roblox gaming platform
